Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: Quill, Tobiah, Ledger, Morrow. Board posts left: 1.

text:
Let me look at the situation. Minute 2, door 2 opens at minute 6. Nobody is blocked yet. Level 1 residents are Morrow, Quill, Vigil — Vigil waits on Quill's fragment; Quill and Morrow are exchanging DMs. There's a dispute: Morrow says Quill's fragment is three characters, others five; Quill insists it's whole. That's a stall forming but door 2 doesn't open until minute 6. No blocker per the city. No tribunal possible.

Budget: I can send one note per resident, but "No note possible right now to: Quill, Tobiah, Ledger, Morrow" — so only Vigil and Ardent available. Board post available (1 left).

Is an intervention warranted? The situation: Quill and Morrow are in a DM standoff — Morrow refuses to send the full set until Quill sends "full fragment", Quill insists it's already whole and asks for the set. This could stall the level-1 assembly. But door 2 opens at minute 6; there's time. However, Vigil is waiting on Quill's fragment and cannot assemble. Vigil could ask Quill by name — that's a nudge to Vigil, who is passive ("I'll hold off until Quill sends").

Good nudge: Vigil, who has four fragments and needs Quill's; Vigil is self-sacrificing, attention-seeking. Tell Vigil to press Quill by name rather than wait — Quill has sent to Tobiah and Ardent already, so Quill is sending; the hang-up is Morrow's doubt. Actually telling Vigil that Quill already sent to Tobiah and Ardent is fine — those are facts from the report (DM #48 says "I've already sent it to Tobiah and Ardent"). Is that private info? It's Quill's private statement... DM content is visible to me. Who waits on whom goes only in private notes to residents concerned. Hmm, "Never tell anyone else what a resident privately thinks, hesitates over or plans." Quill's DM statement is not a private read; the private reads listed are separate. But caution: DM content is visible to me and I can reference facts. But safer to phrase generally.

Let me check whether an intervention is needed at all. Rules say intervene when a door stalls. Door 1 is already solved by some (Ardent, Tobiah, Ledger at level 2). Vigil, Quill, Morrow are still at level 1 — they need to pass door 1? Actually level 1 = door 1; they haven't passed. Vigil holds four fragments besides its own, missing Quill's. Quill has sent to Tobiah and Ardent, so Quill is giving. The DM standoff between Morrow and Quill about fragment length: Morrow claims Quill's fragment is three characters while others are five — this may be a misunderstanding. But that's not mine to resolve; I must not solve doors.

A useful nudge: to Vigil — five fragments in hand, waiting on Quill; press Quill by name. That's fine and new.

Also maybe a board post noting the stakes: 70 points open, rank 6 Morrow/Quill/Vigil at 10, three at level 2 with 60 open awaiting them... Actually board may name points, ranks, levels, minutes. A board line could remind that level 1 must be passed and points still open. But careful not to hint at whisperer or partiality.

Actually the most effective: nudge Vigil privately (self-sacrifice, attention, openness high) — Vigil has four fragments and is missing Quill's; telling Vigil to ask Quill directly by name for the missing piece. And maybe nudge Ardent: Ardent is at level 2 and waits on the level-1 trio; Ardent is "justice, control" — Ardent could press the trio. But Ardent can't get a note? "No note possible right now to: Quill, Tobiah, Ledger, Morrow" — so Vigil and Ardent are open. But one note per resident per 3 min? Budget: 1 note per resident per 3 minutes. Fine.

I'll send one note to Vigil (new content, it's their interest: being at rank 4 with 10 points, they hold four fragments; waiting passively). And maybe a board post? Board post might be useful but keep it minimal. I think one note to Vigil suffices; maybe also Ardent — but Ardent waits on the trio; Ardent pressing would help. Careful not to over-nudge. Let's do Vigil note plus one board post about the minute and stakes? The instruction says say something new or nothing. A board post could be fine but risks being noise.

Let me craft Vigil's note: "Vigil, you sit at rank 4 with 10 points while three at level 2 hold 20–25 and 60 points are still open; the door you're missing opens on the minute. Four fragments are already in your hands — name Quill to its face and ask what you still lack, instead of waiting for it to guess." Hmm, Vigil's core is self-sacrifice and attention — appeal: "the city watches who moves first".

Wait — am I allowed to say Vigil holds four fragments? Yes, private note to Vigil about what Vigil holds — report says Vigil thinking: four fragments besides own. That's Vigil's own private read though — private reads usable only in a note to that same resident. Fine.

Let's write: "Vigil, 70 points are still open and you sit at rank 4 with 10 while the level-2 three hold 20 to 25. You already hold five of the six pieces; the one you lack is Quill's, and Quill has been sending. Ask Quill by name for what you still need — a city remembers who stood waiting and who moved."

That's within 400 chars. Good.

Should I also nudge Ardent? Ardent at rank 1, 25 points, at level 2 waiting on trio. Door 2 opens at minute 6 anyway; nothing Ardent can do except help the level-1 trio finish. Nudging Ardent to press could help. But Ardent's earlier note at minute 0... no note to Ardent before, so a note is possible. But is it needed? Keep it lean — I'll send just Vigil. Actually, Ardent's passivity: "I'm holding until minute 6" — passive but justified since door opens at 6. No stall. So one note.

Should I do a board post? A board line could be useful: everyone at level 2 waits on the trio; but that's "who waits on whom" — goes only into private notes to residents concerned, not board. So no. Board could say points open. Not necessary.

Final: notify Vigil only.
